title: c7b-bind-scenarios-to-surface output (one behavior's bindings)
description: One entry per scenario in one behavior. c9 merges every behavior's output into the pack's behaviors/scenario-bindings.json projection.

conventions_hash.description: Hash of the target-conventions.yaml these bindings were decided against. A conventions change invalidates them, the same way it invalidates c7's operations — bindings are target-side facts, and the target's conventions are their input.

surface.description: rest: observable through a named operation. client-side: observable in the client with no server round-trip (a rendered condition, a navigation outcome that became a route). domain-only: a computation or state change with no client-visible surface, checkable only against the domain layer. not-observable: no equivalent exists in the target at any layer — an open question, not a verdict.

operation_id.description: Required when surface is 'rest'. Must name an operation c7/c8 emitted; this step never composes a path of its own.

expected_status.description: Only when surface is 'rest' and the scenario's Then is an outcome status. Copied from the operation's fragment or from api_conventions.auth_semantics/status_mapping — never chosen here.

rationale.description: Why this surface, in one or two sentences. For anything other than a plain 'rest' binding this is the load-bearing field: it is what an implementer reads instead of re-deriving the decision.

preserves_legacy_meaning.description: False when the target's observable outcome is an adaptation rather than an equivalent — e.g. a legacy 'the login page is redisplayed' observed as a 401. False does not mean wrong; it means the binding is a decision someone could revisit, and it seeds an open-questions entry so that revisiting it is possible.
